spans.content: CHINA OVERSEAS LAND & INVESTMENT (0688.HK)
1H26 Preview: Sector-leading contracts sales growth though margin pressure still lingers; Buy

We update our estimates by 1) on positive side – reflecting stronger-than-expected sales performance in 1H26 (+12% yoy), we raise our 2026E contract sales estimate by 11% to Rmb265bn, implying flattish/+6% yoy in 2H and full-year 26E, ahead of coverage stronger SOE average of -7%/-4%. As a result, we revise up our DP revenue forecast by an average 2% for 2026E-28E, with total revenue expected to see only a modest decline; 2) on negative side – we lower 2026E-28E DP gross margin by average 1pp and now expecting 14pp GPM for 2026E, which is closer to the mid-point of management’s beginning-of-year estimates (i.e 13%-15%) amid ongoing pricing pressure outside of top-tier cities. That said, we believe COLI remains one of the best-positioned developers in our coverage, supported by a high-quality landbank (over 80% Tier-1/2 exposure and lowest aged inventory among coverage), limiting near-term impairment risk. As a result, we lower our core earnings estimate by average 5%, with 2026E core EPS expected to decline 6%, followed by recovery from 2027E as margins stabilize. Our revised topline and core earnings forecasts are 5% and 4% below Datastream consensus, respectively, and our 12-month NAV-based target price remains unchanged at HK$14.7 (still at a 10% NAV discount). Maintain Buy.

1H contract sales solid while landbanking sequentially slowed down: COLI's 1H26 contract sales recorded at a solid +12% yoy to Rmb134bn, ahead of our stronger SOE coverage average of flattish, riding on strong sales performance by high-end/luxury projects with prime locations in T1 cities. On the other hand, we note COLI's 1H26 land investment only accounted for HSD% of contract sales, below c.50% in FY25, 40% GSe for full-year 26E and mid-twenties% of our tracked SOE developers' average during 1H26. That said, we estimate project-level GPMs for new land acquisition in 1H26 remain competitive at c.29% (5pp above tracked developers' average). Our view on 1H26: we expect roughly a low-teen% yoy core income decline in 1H26, reflecting a moderate yoy dip in the topline, aligning with the broader industry trend and our full-year 26E projection and approx. 1pp yoy DP GPM decline given continued property price weakness outside top-tier cities.
■ Keys to watch next: 1) For upcoming 1H26 earnings - management guidance on potential inventory impairment and profitability impacts, especially considering

Investment Thesis

We are positive on China Overseas Land & Investment given its shares have priced in the highest impairment loss among SOE (state-owned enterprise) peers, which we consider is unjustified given COLI's peer-leading asset quality and liquidity position. With liquidity pressure continuing to weigh on the industry (particularly on privately owned enterprises), we believe COLI is best positioned to take share from POEs. We expect COLI's share price to continue to outperform on the back of its strong balance sheet to capture low-cost investment for future growth amid an unsettled industry environment. We also expect COLI to achieve more resilient sales and margin performance supported by quality landbank exposure and a healthy liquidity condition. We also see the most attractive total returns, in terms of dividend yield, among our coverage SOE coverage. We are Buy rated on COLI.

GS Factor Profile

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
